seo.title: Null Invaders: a browser shooter you play on the page
seo.description: Fly an interceptor through a real webpage: shoot letters into binary, break button factories and clear four waves. Free in your browser.

sections.heading: Null Invaders
sections.body: Fly an interceptor through a real webpage. Shoot letters into binary, break the button factories, and clear the aliens they release over four waves. It plays right here in your browser: no install, and Recall gives the page back.

spans.text: Play it here, then make it part of your own project. Visit GitHub for the source code, setup instructions, and integration examples.

image.alt: Null Invaders in play on its own DOM VIRUS page: the interceptor flies over the page, the title is shot into binary and the scoreboard shows Trident online

items.title: Press Play
items.body: The interceptor launches over this page. Buttons become alien factories, and the headings and paragraphs are the battlefield.

items.title: Fly and fire
items.body: Steer with the mouse, WASD or the arrow keys, and hold click or Space to fire. On a phone the thumbstick flies and the round Fire key shoots; hold both together.

items.title: Upgrade your gun
items.body: Combat XP upgrades the weapon during the run. Pulse starts with one shot; Twin unlocks at 8 XP, Trident at 24 and four-shot Overdrive at 50.

items.title: Break the factories
items.body: Shoot a button until its health level drains. A destroyed factory stops spawning for the rest of that wave; factories reactivate between waves.

items.title: Clear four waves
items.body: You have three shields. Finish wave four to clear the page. Press Escape or Recall at any time to give the page back.

items.title: Shoot the text
items.body: A letter gives 1 XP and keeps the three-second combo window open, so page text is the quickest way to the next weapon tier.

items.title: Chain your kills
items.body: Three chained alien kills raise the combo multiplier, up to ×5. Losing a shield clears the combo but keeps your weapon.

items.title: Hit the factories
items.body: A factory hit gives 2 XP and a destroyed factory another 8, and it shuts that spawn source for the wave.

items.title: Keep moving
items.body: The squid is the fastest alien shape, and alien health rises with the wave. G jumps to the next factory; P pauses.

items.title: Right on 2× and zoomed screens
items.body: On a 1.5× or 2× screen, the ship, the invaders and the factories' beacon rings used to draw 1.5–2× too big. Now they sit exactly on the page.

items.title: The scoreboard drags
items.body: Grab the scoreboard anywhere that isn't a key, with mouse or touch. It stays inside the window, also when the window shrinks.

items.title: Readable keys
items.body: The scoreboard's key labels pass WCAG AA contrast in both light and dark themes.

items.title: On the Fizlet engine
items.body: Since 1.0.0, Null Invaders runs on the Fizlet engine with the same rules and numbers, and a scoreboard in the Board UI kit.

items.question: Do I need to install anything to play Null Invaders?
items.answer: No. Null Invaders plays on this page in your browser. Press Play, and press Escape or Recall when you are done to give the page back.

items.question: Can I play Null Invaders on a phone?
items.answer: Yes. Phones get a thumbstick to fly and a round Fire key, and you can hold both at once.

items.question: What happens to the page when I play?
items.answer: Shots write a literal 0 or 1 into the page's own text, and buttons become alien factories. Recall restores what the game changed and still owns.

items.question: Can I put Null Invaders on my own site?
items.answer: Yes. It is open source (MIT). The GitHub repository has the source code, setup instructions and integration examples.
